clue.text: It gets patients high

parts.note: the vehicle that lifts sick people into the sky to carry them to hospital

explanation.surface: Something that makes people under medical care feel elated, like a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets patients high' suggests narcotics; read literally, it is a flying vehicle that takes patients up into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft equipped to carry the sick or injured literally raises patients aloft.

clue.text: Firm has corrupt data about staff

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the staff piece
corrupt data has been scrambled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to staff a desk is to man it

explanation.surface: A company has damaged information concerning its employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business, but it is the adjective; 'staff' is the verb, to man a post, not the noun for employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone firm in a position is unyielding, refusing to be moved.

clue.text: Compensate for what nudists do eventually

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make amends for a wrong
second meaning: read as ..., to put clothes on again

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as re-dress: naturists must get dressed again at some point.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a grievance is to remedy or make up for it.

clue.text: Flyer produced by master with Napoleon complex

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in the MA degree or a ship's master

indicators.note: complex here means intricately knotted, so the letters of the emperor's name are tangled up

explanation.surface: An aircraft made by a craftsman who believes he is the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Napoleon complex' is a phrase about touchy short men, but here 'complex' is the anagram signal acting on the emperor's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyer is anything that flies; a single-winged aeroplane is one.

clue.text: Dumb loyalty regularly needed to serve on such a vessel

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the phrase, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Silent obedience is what a submarine crew needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of 'Dumb loyalty'. The surface fits a German wartime submarine, where silence and loyalty mattered.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, the kind of vessel on which such discipline was demanded.

clue.text: Restless French film director turned up during a shot

indicators.note: during puts the reversed name in the middle of the attempt

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a shot at something

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up reads the director's name from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: Jacques Tati, the French director of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday

explanation.surface: A jittery French filmmaker arrived while a scene was being filmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests filming but means an attempt, a go; 'turned up' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction meaning agitated, played in a restless, hurried manner.

clue.text: Vital force opposing Italian region

parts.note: chi (qi) is the life energy of Chinese philosophy
anti means against

explanation.surface: A strong life energy resists a part of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is the Tuscan hill area that gives its name to the wine.

clue.text: It has grocer's unusual story of path to fortune

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of these three words appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A tale with a shopkeeper's odd account of how he became wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It has' looks like a link to the rest, but those letters are part of the fodder: IT HAS GROCERS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a tale of someone rising from poverty to great wealth.

clue.text: Drop first-class group game

parts.note: A, as in A1 or grade A, means first-class
a band is a musical group
game, as in willing, means on: 'I'm on for that'

explanation.surface: Remove a top-rated team's match from the schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a plan is to give it up entirely, to abandon it.

clue.text: Vacancy after one replaces Head of Equities for expressing views

indicators.note: replaces swaps the numeral in for the letter it ousts

parts.note: an opening is a job vacancy

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word, Equities

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A finance post was filled after its leading equities man was replaced, prompting comment.
explanation.walkthrough: OPENING has its E (head of Equities) replaced by I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, so the participle describes someone voicing them.

clue.text: Redesign faded green on first couple's home

indicators.note: redesign means arrange afresh, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden makeover instruction: rework the washed-out lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve, the Bible's first pair of humans, lived in paradise before the Fall.

clue.text: Ask for assistance reportedly for ocean vegetation

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is spoken and the result spelt differently

parts.note: to ask for assistance is to seek help

explanation.surface: Request help when dealing with plants growing in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp is a large brown seaweed that grows in marine waters.

clue.text: One covers sporting legend broken up

definitions.text: One covers sporting legend broken up

parts.words: One covers sporting legend broken up
parts.note: split legend into leg end, i.e. the foot: this sports shoe covers an athlete's foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting legend' suggests a famous athlete; 'broken up' tells you to split it into leg end, the foot, which a sports shoe covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a running or gym shoe, so it encloses the foot of someone doing sport.

clue.text: He was reportedly tight as he made up plot!

definitions.text: He was reportedly tight as he made up plot!

parts.words: He was reportedly tight as he made up plot!
parts.note: his first name sounds like 'tight as', and he invented the Popish Plot of 1678

explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates fabricated the Popish Plot, a supposed Catholic conspiracy against Charles II; 'reportedly tight as' is a sound-alike for his first name, not a claim he was drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The English perjurer invented a fictitious conspiracy that led to many executions.

clue.text: Doctor paid her to be a symbol of love

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician paid a woman to pose as an emblem of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician but is the verb, to tamper: PAID HER TO rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite was the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Strike march to have the most popular records released

parts.note: to strike is to hit
a parade is a march

explanation.surface: Workers walk out and demonstrate to get the top songs issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike march' suggests industrial action; it is two separate synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is the chart of best-selling music singles.

clue.text: Person in the job is popular, with Latin flair

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
cum is the Latin word for with
a bent is a natural talent or flair

explanation.surface: An office-holder is well liked and has a gift for Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The incumbent is whoever currently holds an office or post.

clue.text: Denounce Conservative guarantee

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A politician condemns a Tory pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To censure is to criticise formally and harshly.

clue.text: High-class glove Spooner found in front of stage

indicators.note: Spooner, the don famed for swapping word starts, signals exchanging the opening sounds

parts.note: posh means upper-class
a mitt is a glove

explanation.surface: An upmarket glove turns up near the front of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of POSH MITT gives MOSH PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The mosh pit is the area just before a concert stage where fans dance wildly.

clue.text: Old style piece found in treasure trove

indicators.note: a piece found in the words is a run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An antique item turns up among buried riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes fashions that imitate those of an earlier era.

clue.text: Achieve success in port wine making technique

indicators.note: in places the success word inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
to pass is to succeed, as in an exam

explanation.surface: Doing well in a fortified wine from Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine but is a harbour city, RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripasso is a Valpolicella method of refermenting wine over leftover grape skins.

clue.text: One under 12 supplies some of the extra I need

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sports coach provides part of what an athlete requires.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' refers to the answer at 12 across, a coach: the one under him is his pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone under a trainer's instruction is a learner being taught.

clue.text: Worker, with pride perhaps, surrenders

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
pride is one of the seven deadly sins, an example of a sin

explanation.surface: A labourer, perhaps too proud, gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand in, as in handing in weapons, is to yield or submit something.

clue.text: Obsessives who knew murder cases by heart

indicators.note: the heart of each word is its centre, so the middle letters of the three words are taken

explanation.surface: Fanatics who had memorised every detail of homicide trials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By heart' reads as memorised but asks for the centres: NE, RD and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerds are people fixated on a niche interest, absorbed to the point of obsession.

clue.text: Soothe pulse during recess

indicators.note: during puts the seed inside the church recess

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess in a church
a pea is a pulse, an edible seed

explanation.surface: Calm a racing heartbeat over the holiday break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like the heartbeat but is a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease is to pacify or placate, calming someone down.

clue.text: Upset travellers come back carrying silverware

indicators.note: carrying means holding the trophy inside
come back reads the travellers word in the reverse direction

parts.note: reps are travelling sales representatives
a cup is a trophy, sporting silverware

explanation.surface: Disappointed tourists return holding a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travellers' are commercial travellers, sales reps, not tourists; 'Upset' is a verb, to wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck or thwart it, upsetting it.

clue.text: I left playwright during fantastic time away

indicators.note: during puts the shortened name inside the word for fantastic

parts.note: ace means excellent, fantastic

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter I goes from the dramatist's name

parts.note: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian dramatist

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a dramatist during a wonderful holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as a direction but means departed: the Norwegian playwright loses his I before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An absence is a period of being away, as from school or work.

clue.text: What supposedly makes a man check out damaged store unit

parts.note: to check out is to test

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: one is a single unit

explanation.surface: Inspect the damaged items in a shop unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' reads as a shop premises but simply means one; 'check out' is a single verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The male sex hormone is popularly credited with masculine traits; 'supposedly' hedges the cliché.
